subject: DPA redline + SCCs: locality exceptions & technical safeguards
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@acmeops.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline + SCCs: initial technical safeguards questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the call last week. Attached is AcmeOps' redline to the DPA (AcmeOps_DPA_v3_redline.docx) and a proposed mapping to the 2021 SCCs (SCCs_mapping_20260629.xlsx). A few open items we want to surface early so we can keep the timeline to sign by ~10 July: 

- Data locality / exception: we have an operations requirement to restrict processed EU personal data to EU-hosted instances unless an explicit transfer impact addendum is accepted. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a narrow locality exception for our account and, if not, propose mitigations.

- Key management/KMS: the DPA asks for customer-managed keys (section 4.2). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer KMS/HSM integration for Dedicated and Private deployments, and if so what evidence you can share (KMS integration guide, architecture diagram, SOC2 control mapping).

- Subprocessors: redline includes a clause requiring notice + 30-day objection window for new subprocessors. Please provide the current subprocessor list and indicate which subprocessors (if any) are used for logging/analytics. We also attached a zip with export-control documents we rely on for onboarding (export-controls-evidence.zip).

- SCCs & transfer impact assessment: we included our initial SCCs mapping. If Redwood prefers a different SCC module, please propose language in the DPA and confirm Redwood’s position on Addendum/Annex approach vs standalone Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA).

We’re copying LegalOps for contract tracking. If you could get an internal owner assigned (legal/tech/security) and confirm next steps today, that would be great.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
AcmeOps

[attachments: AcmeOps_DPA_v3_redline.docx (document), SCCs_mapping_20260629.xlsx (spreadsheet), export-controls-evidence.zip (archive)]

Subject: RE: DPA redline + SCCs: locality exceptions & technical safeguards

Team — forwarding AcmeOps’ redline and SCCs mapping. Key ask is whether we can accept a scoped EU-locality exception and what tech safeguards/evidence we can provide to make the transfer risk palatable. Proposed split of work: 

- Marissa: lead on SCCs mapping and speak to whether we can offer the standalone TIA vs annex approach. Please propose redline language for either option.
- Rishi: validate KMS/HSM support surface and produce a 1-page evidence pack (KMS integration options, SOC2 control references, encryption-in-transit-at-rest statements). Also confirm whether any Dedicated/Private customers are already using CMK/HSM and any constraints.
- Kimberly: coordinate order form ramifications if we accept a locality carveout (pricing/hosting SLA changes). Also flag any billing/region implications.

Timeline suggestion: 
- Today (29 Jun): internal review assignments completed and initial replies to Elena acknowledging receipt (I’ve done that).
- Wed 1 Jul: Marissa + Rishi send proposed language and evidence pack.
- Fri 3 Jul: internally agree version to send back to AcmeOps.
- Mon 6 Jul: target counter-sign activities / legal sync.

Cc'ing AcmeOps so they see owners. Elena — we’ll come back with the redline and an evidence bundle by EOD Wed (1 Jul). If you have a strict 10 Jul sign target we’ll prioritize off-cycle.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Legal (Contracts & Privacy)
Redwood Inference

- I’ve uploaded a narrow export-controls reconciliation (export-controls-evidence.zip) and added a short note requesting that Redwood mark any subprocessor that will see exported data (logging/monitoring providers).
